_doc: How long each part lasts without an input before it dies. days = midpoint of range. basis says what kind of figure it is: lethal (a published mortality figure), observed (the longest survival seen in studies; no published lethal limit, so the real limit may be longer), derived (worked out from published data, with the method in source). Sourced 2026-10-15.

hen.source: Merck Veterinary Manual: water deprivation over 36 hours causes a marked increase in mortality of mature poultry; Poultry Science review (PMC10203017): water-deprived White Leghorn hens survived 6 days on average at 29 C. Heat shortens this.

Poultry Science (PMID 11469648): hens came through 8-14 days of feed withdrawal; PMID 10735746: Hy-Line W-36 hens reached 35% body-weight loss around day 19-21 of withdrawal. These are welfare limits from forced-molting trials, not lethal limits.

cow.source: Journal of Agricultural Science (2002): Friesian cattle went through 3 days of total water deprivation; lactating cows lost about 12% live weight and 30% milk after 48 hours (PMID 8946484). No published lethal limit found.

goat.source: Bedouin goats went through 4 days of water deprivation, losing 23-32% body weight (PMID 6141035); Nubian goats survived 4 days without food and water (FAO AGRIS). Desert breeds; no published lethal limit found.
Nubian goats survived 4 days without food (FAO AGRIS); adult dwarf goats were fasted 7 days in a study (PMID 2272603). No published lethal limit found.

sheep.source: Dorper sheep went 5 days without water in heat, losing 16.7% body mass (PLoS ONE 2015, PMC4326457). No published lethal limit found.

tomato.source: Derived from FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, ch. 8: tomato total available water 72-136 mm (loamy sand to silt) used up at 6 mm/day, the paper's example peak crop water use. Hotter weather empties the soil faster.

lettuce.source: Derived from FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, ch. 8: lettuce root zone 0.3-0.5 m holds 27-85 mm of available water, used up at 6 mm/day. Lettuce is the most sensitive of the three crops.

corn.source: Derived from FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, ch. 8: maize total available water 108-204 mm (loamy sand to silt) used up at 6 mm/day. Seedlings and sandy soil die much sooner.
